Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the exciting chase! The umpires are in position and the Indian players have taken their places on the field. It will be the pairing of Ryan Rickelton and Reeza Hendricks to open the innings for South Africa. Arshdeep Singh will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, records galore in that thunderous first innings but the game is only half done. South Africa will be eyeing up a few records of their own as the crowd in Johannesburg braces themselves for more heavy hitting. Can South Africa do the impossible? Or will India get the job done with the ball? Find out soon as the run chase is up next.

South Africa knew they were going to be up against it but this is not what they would have expected and simply had no answer for the carnage. Marco Jansen bowled more than decently up top and at the death as well but an early injury to Gerald Coetzee forced Markram's hand and the spinners as well as the inexperienced pacers, went for plenty of runs in the middle overs. There were a couple of dropped chances that cost them dearly but in reality, it was total annihilation.

Everyone knows the ball flies here at the Bullring given the height it is located at above sea level by the Indian batters took that to another level. Abhishek Sharma was the aggressor early on as Sanju Samson also kept hitting the ball sweetly from the other end but once Sharma got out, the duo of Samson and Tilak Varma went completely berserk. They hit a total of 23 sixes, the second-most in a T20I innings as both batters hit their second tons of the series and they were just unbelievably good. Their stand remained unbeaten at 210 runs, the highest for the 2nd wicket in all T20Is.

Talk about a demolition job and the Wanderers has once again witnessed some scintillating batting action as the sixes kept pouring in and India have ended up posting a mammoth total of 283 runs, the highest-ever at this ground in T20Is.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! This is carnage from the Indian openers! Slower again and dug in short over middle and leg, sits up nicely for the batter. Abhishek Sharma waits back and muscles it high and handsome over the mid-wicket fence for another biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Andile Simelane to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! A bit slower but spilled down the leg side for another wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Andile Simelane to Abhishek Sharma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: The ball seems to have been lost here and the umpires are changing it.

SIX! Andile Simelane is greeted with a lusty blow from Abhishek Sharma. Hard length wide of the off stump, Sharma steps out and backs away before lifting it over deep cover for a biggie. That's gone out of the ground!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Andile Simelane to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Andile Simelane comes into the attack now.
Grunts in and serves a wide yorker, taking some pace off the ball as well. Abhishek Sharma reaches out and squeezes it past point for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Lutho Sipamla to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller in length on off and middle, Samson pushes it out wide of covers for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Lutho Sipamla to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Swung away over the ropes! Poor delivery, slower and shorter, sitting up nicely for the batter. Sanju Samson picks up the pace early and clobbers it over deep mid-wicket for another biggie. India racing along now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Lutho Sipamla to Sanju Samson, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: That's gone a long way up but will land safely. Slower one, fuller and angled into leg, Sanju Samson backs away early and decides to go big but skews it straight over mid off for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Lutho Sipamla to Sanju Samson, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! An agricultural heave but the outfield is lightning fast. Good length at the stumps, angling in, Sanju Samson looks to hit down the ground but it comes off the inner half of the blade and goes through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Lutho Sipamla to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Lutho Sipamla begins from over the wicket and pitches the ball up around off, Samson plays a good cover drive off the front foot but fails to beat the cover fielder to his left.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Lutho Sipamla to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good change-up from Jansen but 14 runs come off that over. Banged in again and around off but it is the slower one, Sharma comes forward to take on the pull but is well beaten
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Up, up and away! Short ball at the body, hurrying the batter a bit but Abhishek Sharma manages to get under it and pulls it over deep backward square leg for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten again! Banged into the deck over middle, angling it in, Abhishek Sharma backs away to open up the off side but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Banged into the deck around off, this one seamed away as well with some extra bounce. Sharma tries to pull but is well beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Excellent chase from Gerald Coetzee. Hard length again, angled into the batter, Abhishek Sharma makes room and launches the ball over mid on. Coetzee runs after it and slides in to save a couple of runs for his side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FIVE WIDES! South Africa's woes with the extras continue. Hard length, starting on middle and leg and this one just angles a long way down leg, no chance for the keeper and it will be five free runs for India.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Nagging length, around the top of off and angling away, Samson hangs back and backs away a bit before tapping the ball on its head, guiding it to deep third for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Marco Jansen to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up again around off, Sharma gets across the off stump, looking to lift it over mid on but miscues it straight to the fielder there.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Gerald Coetzee to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches the ball further up and takes pace off as well, Samson stays back and pushes it through the gap at covers for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Gerald Coetzee to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Wonderful hands from Sanju Samson! Back of a length around off, shaping back in as well, Samson presses back and cuts it late, using the pace of the ball to get it behind point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Gerald Coetzee to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Goes short again but falters with the line as this one is angled down the leg side for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Gerald Coetzee to Sanju Samson, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Much better from Coetzee! Short again but bowled with much more intent and a tad shorter around off, Sanju Samson has to hop trying to play it away but is beaten for pace and bounce.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Gerald Coetzee to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! Dug in short but without any intent, sits up nicely for the batter over off, Sanju Samson has ample time to hang back and get on top of the bounce, smashing it well over deep mid-wicket for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Gerald Coetzee to Sanju Samson, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: On the money! Good length, on a tight line on off stump and extracts a bit of additional bounce as well. Sanju Samson tentatively fends it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Gerald Coetzee to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A slight halt in play here as Abhishek Sharma has been struck on the helmet and a mandatory concussion check will now follow. The physio comes out and thankfully, everything is fine and we are good to continue. Also, Gerald Coetzee comes in to bowl from the other end.

Ouch! That's a nasty delivery from Marco Jansen and he is fired up! Brings out a quick bumper now, banging it in over off stump, this one hurries on and climbs up. Abhishek Sharma is taken by surprise as he looks to pull and seems to have got a top edge straight into the helmet.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Streaky once again! Hard length around the top of off, Sanju Samson looks to punch but gets an inside edge past leg stump for one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Marco Jansen to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: PUT DOWN! Marco Jansen could have easily had two in two but Reeza Hendricks has spilled that sharp chance. Full and quick at 143 clicks outside off, Abhishek Sharma looks to jam it out but gets a thick outside edge that goes fast towards first slip and Hendricks can't react in time, trying to catch it around his face. They get a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Samson avoids a third straight duck, just though! Cross-seamer from Jansen, full and around off, angling away, Samson pushes at it and gets an outside edge that travels well wide of first slip and goes down to deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Marco Jansen to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, aimed right at the middle stump line, Samson watches it well and plays it late, blocking it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Marco Jansen to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Much better! Slightly fuller on middle and leg, swinging back in, Sanju Samson gets forward and just tucks it away to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Marco Jansen to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! That's loose from Marco Jansen to begin with! Hard length on leg, drifts down the leg side for a wide, the 24th one from South Africa in this series.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Marco Jansen to Sanju Samson, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to get the play underway! The sun is shining and the umpires have taken their places on the field. The players of South Africa are also spreading out on the field as the duo of Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma make their way out to the middle to open the innings for India. Marco Jansen will take the new ball and he is raring to go. Let's play...

Just a few minutes left for the start of this final game but first, the two sets of players walk out to the middle along with the mascots and lineup for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of India first, followed by that of South Africa.

Aiden Markram, the captain of South Africa says that they weren't too sure and were leaning towards batting first. Adds that they haven't been able to output at their best in all three departments but is excited at the opportunity to change that tonight. Mentions that they just have to level the series and were able to level it up from 1-0 down and ultimately it is up to the execution.

Suryakumar Yadav, India's captain, says that he is going to bat first and he will try to implement the same things from the pevious two matches. Adds that the plan is very clear where they put runs on the board and try to defend them. Concludes that these things happen in the short form of cricket and the series is on the line so they as a team have to put in their best efforts. Also informs that they are going in with the same team.

India (Unchanged XI) - Sanju Samson (WK), Abhishek Sharma, Tilak Varma, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Hardik Pandya, Rinku Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh, Ravi Bishnoi, Varun Chakaravarthy.

South Africa (Unchanged XI) - Ryan Rickelton, Reeza Hendricks, Aiden Markram (C), Tristan Stubbs, Heinrich Klaasen (WK), David Miller, Marco Jansen, Gerald Coetzee, Andile Simelane, Keshav Maharaj, Lutho Sipamla.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of Suryakumar Yadav and India will BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Natalie Germanos is pitchside. She starts by saying that it is a slightly cooler day than normal and mentions that it is the center pitch. Adds that the straight boundary is massive at 56 meters with 62 meters and 66 meters on either side. Shaun Pollock joins her and says that the surface looks really good as it has a thick covering of grass with barely any cracks which means it will carry through nicely. Reckons that once the batters start middling a couple of balls, they could really pile on.

Right then, the series is secured for India but they won't be happy to share it with South Africa, who on the other hand, will be eager to finish off on a high. There's also a forecast for a bit of rain before the start of the game but let's hope that stays away and we get a full game in. Toss and team news in a bit, stay tuned.

South Africa on the other hand, will surely try to get redemption for the World Cup Final loss by at least drawing this series. In the batting department, Tristan Stubbs has been brilliant and even Heinrich Klaasen had a good game last time around after an underwhelming first two games. Aiden Markaram as captain has been good but as a batter, he hasn’t been able to fire with the bat and the only consistent player has been Marco Jansen who will be crucial with both bat and ball in hand.

For India, the year 2024 has been prolific in the shortest format where they became the World Champions by defeating South Africa in the final. They have also won 23 games out of 25 in T20Is this year and will look to make it 24 wins out of 26 come the end of this game. India will likely field the same eleven from the previous game but the spotlight will be on Sanju Samson who has a couple of ducks after a couple of T20 tons and the Indian skipper, Suryakumar Yadav who hasn't got going in this series. On the bowling front, Arshdeep Singh and Varun Chakaravarthy will be key.

Hello, and a very warm welcome to the coverage of the 4th and final T20I between South Africa and India from the Wanderers Stadium, Johannesburg. India are leading in the series by 2-1 at the moment and they will look forward to taking the trophy home by winning this match. On the other hand, South Africa would want to win this match to level up the series at 2-2. An exciting game is on the cards.
